inputs.name: Day: covariance set to zero by fiat
Athos via Day: P(fix) = x0 wrong for real populations
Day Z23188201: 1/(2N) exact for any offspring distribution
keruru exact chains: 1/(2N_census) to 15 decimals; Ne 5.6x lower

day.reading: real populations have genotype-reproduction covariance; x0 answers the no-covariance problem
day.why_none: Day and Athos name the covariance but give no value; the record shows what any c != 0 does (2.17x and 1.18x at c = +0.05; 0.32x and 0.84x at c = -0.05)

critic.reading: a neutral allele has c = 0 by definition; then P(fix) = x0 under any offspring distribution

notes: With c = 0, P(fix) = i/2N to 1e-12 in both chains, including the sweepstakes chain with Ne 5.6x below N (keruru's result; Day's Z23188201 sentence). With c != 0 the allele frequency has a drift term, which is selection, and P(fix) moves off 1/(2N). The arithmetic of both readings is fixed; whether a neutral allele can carry covariance is the definitional dispute.
